issues.legal_issue: A will surrounded by suspicious circumstances is not proved unless the propounder dispels those circumstances through satisfactory evidence of due execution and attestation.
material_facts: The will gave the testator’s entire property to the propounder, a distant relation, while providing only unspecified maintenance for the testator’s widow and sister and nothing for his daughter or nearer relations.
The propounder took part in the will’s execution and was its principal beneficiary.
The testator’s signature on the will differed from his usual signature, and the ink appeared different from that used for the body of the document.
The testator used to sign blank papers for court cases, which could have been available to people connected with the will’s preparation.
Only three attesting witnesses were produced from the sixteen who had signed the will; the witnesses produced were interested in the propounder, while independent witnesses were not called.
The witnesses gave contradictory accounts on material matters, and their evidence did not satisfactorily establish due execution and attestation.
issues.conclusion: The propounder did not prove due execution and attestation or dispel the suspicious circumstances, so the will could not support a grant of letters of administration.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, a will must meet the special requirements for execution and attestation. As explained in H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B. N. Thimmajamma, the propounder bears the burden of proving the will; where suspicious circumstances exist, the propounder must remove them to the court’s satisfaction through clear and satisfactory evidence. The propounder’s benefit from the will and participation in its execution may themselves be suspicious circumstances.

rule.if: probate_proceeding and suspicious_circumstances and propounder_benefits and interested_attestors_only and independent_attestors_not_called and witness_accounts_conflicted

predicates.probate_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding seeking authority to administer an estate on the basis of a will.
predicates.suspicious_circumstances: The will contains an unnatural distribution, an unusual testator signature, or other circumstances raising doubt about whether it reflects the testator’s act and intention.
predicates.propounder_benefits: The person seeking to establish the will receives a substantial benefit under it and takes part in its execution.
predicates.interested_attestors_only: The witnesses produced to prove execution have connections or interests that make them not independent of the person seeking to establish the will.
predicates.independent_attestors_not_called: Other available witnesses who could provide independent evidence of execution are not produced.
predicates.witness_accounts_conflicted: The evidence of the witnesses produced contains material contradictions or otherwise fails to establish execution and attestation reliably.
predicates.will_execution_not_proved: The will’s due execution and attestation have not been established.

issues.definition: When a will is challenged in a probate proceeding and suspicious circumstances combine with an interested and incomplete or conflicting body of attestation evidence, its execution is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: Registration of a will does not by itself dispel suspicions about its execution unless the evidence shows that the testator knew the document was a will and acknowledged its execution.
material_facts: The will was registered after an application for registration on commission was made by the testator’s representative, and a clerk rather than the registering officer went to the testator.

The evidence did not show that the will was read to the testator or that he read it, or otherwise establish that he knew the document whose execution he was admitting was a will disposing of his property.
The clerk gave only a general account that the testator admitted execution, and the identifying witness did not establish that the testator acknowledged the will to him or signed in his presence.
The evidence surrounding the original execution already contained substantial suspicious circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The registration evidence was insufficient to dispel the suspicions, and registration alone did not establish the will’s genuineness.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the burden described in H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B. N. Thimmajamma, registration may support a will’s genuineness but does not automatically remove suspicions. It can dispel doubt when the evidence shows that the testator understood that the document was a will, admitted its execution, and signed in token of that admission. Registration performed perfunctorily without establishing the testator’s awareness has little value. The Court referred to Vellasaway Sarvai v. L. Sivaraman Servai, Surendra Nath Lahiri v. Jnanendra Nath Lahiri, and Girji Datt Singh v. Gangotri Datt Singh in noting that registration does not invariably establish that a will is genuine.

rule.if: probate_proceeding and suspicious_circumstances and will_registered and registration_process_perfunctory and testator_awareness_not_established

predicates.probate_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding seeking authority to administer an estate on the basis of a will.
predicates.suspicious_circumstances: The circumstances surrounding the will raise a substantial doubt about its execution or genuineness.
predicates.will_registered: The document relied on as a will was registered.
predicates.registration_process_perfunctory: The registration evidence gives only a cursory account of acknowledgment and does not show meaningful verification of the testator’s understanding.
predicates.testator_awareness_not_established: The evidence does not show that the testator knew the document he acknowledged was a will disposing of his property.
predicates.registration_does_not_remove_suspicion: Registration is insufficient to dispel the suspicions surrounding the will.

issues.definition: Where a challenged will is registered but the testator’s understanding of the document is not established by the registration evidence, registration does not remove existing suspicions.

issues.legal_issue: A propounder’s burden to prove due execution and attestation is not discharged merely because the challenger does not expressly allege forgery or another claimant accepts the will.
material_facts: The challengers required the propounder to strictly prove due and legal execution and attestation, and an issue was framed on that matter.
A different claimant accepted the will while relying on a separate will that the courts had found not genuine.
The High Court treated the parties’ pleadings and the other claimant’s acceptance as reasons why further proof of execution and attestation was unnecessary.
issues.conclusion: The pleadings and the other claimant’s acceptance did not excuse the propounder from proving due execution and attestation, particularly in the presence of suspicious circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: The propounder’s burden under section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, and the principles in H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B. N. Thimmajamma, remains where execution and attestation are put in issue and strict proof is demanded. A failure to label the will a forgery is not an admission of due execution, and another claimant’s acceptance cannot replace satisfactory proof for the challengers.

rule.if: probate_proceeding and execution_contested and strict_proof_demanded and other_claimant_accepts_will and other_claimant_relies_on_will_found_not_genuine

predicates.probate_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding seeking authority to administer an estate on the basis of a will.
predicates.execution_contested: A challenger disputes whether the will was duly executed and attested.
predicates.strict_proof_demanded: The challenger puts the propounder to proof of due and legal execution and attestation.
predicates.other_claimant_accepts_will: A different claimant accepts the will whose execution is disputed.
predicates.other_claimant_relies_on_will_found_not_: That claimant relies on a separate will that has been found not genuine.
predicates.propounder_must_still_prove_execution: The person seeking to establish the will remains responsible for proving its due execution and attestation.

issues.definition: When execution is contested and strict proof is demanded, another claimant’s acceptance of the will does not discharge the propounder’s burden, including when that claimant relies on a separate will found not genuine.
